quests.title: Landing Fee
quests.description:
Tollkeeper Nizzik sits halfway down the only ramp into Booty Bay, which means she does not have to chase anybody for anything. Four silver to set foot on the boards, or four hours of work, and she will take either without preference.

The four hours are not made up to punish you. The cart track on the apron above the gate has raptors on it that have learned a crate means food, and the carters have started leaving loads at the treeline rather than argue with them.
quests.accept_text:
Landing fee. You have already landed, so we are only arguing about the amount, and I will save you the trouble: it is four silver and it has been four silver since the road closed.

No coin, then work. Go back up the ramp and clear the apron. Eight of them off the cart track and walk the whole apron, not the first ten yards of it. I will mark you paid when the carters stop leaving loads in the trees.
quests.turn_in_text:
Paid. You are on the boards and nobody can put you off them, which is the whole of what you bought.

And before you ask: no, I do not keep a book of who comes up this ramp. The Baron has never asked me to and I have never offered. The fee is the same whoever is holding it out. That is not a courtesy, it is a schedule, but you will not get even the schedule in Ratchet.

quests.title: Nothing Leaves This Cove
quests.description:
Baron Revilgaz does not rule Booty Bay. He decides which hulls leave on which tide, which after three years turns out to be the same thing, and he has never once said the word out loud.

There is a Bloodsail camp on the south beach and he wants a number off it. He has already been given four numbers by four people with four reasons to shade them.
quests.accept_text:
I will do this slowly, because everybody has it wrong and most of them keep it. A hull that does not arrive costs me the cargo, the berth, and the next three captains who hear about it. Pirates are not a romance down here, they are a column.

There is a camp on the sand at the far end of the shallows. Go and stand in it and count what is standing up. Then come back and tell me the number you counted, not the number you think I want.
quests.turn_in_text:
Forty-one. I had forty-one from the harbourmaster on Tuesday and I have had thirty, sixty and a hundred from people who wanted something.

So you can count and you will say a number that does not flatter anybody. That is rarer on these boards than courage and I pay better for it. Go and see Weezel. He has been waiting three years for somebody who will listen.

quests.title: The Company Has Not Lost This Port
quests.description:
Factor Weezel has an office on the upper gallery, a seal, a ledger, and the Steamwheedle Cartel's authority over this harbour, and he will tell you at length that none of those has been formally withdrawn.

He is right about the law and he knows exactly what the law is worth on these boards. What he wants is a complaint carried to Ratchet by somebody who is not on the Baron's payroll, and a countersigned reply brought back, which he says will settle it.

objectives.label: Put the Cartel's complaint in Customs Officer Prynn's hand

quests.accept_text:
Forty-first week. The harbour book that the Baron's clerk keeps is not a legal instrument, it is a diary, and I have said so in writing every week since the road closed.

Take this to Ratchet and put it in front of customs. They will countersign it and that countersignature is the whole port. You would not know a Cartel seal from a wax blot, which is why you are perfect for the errand: nobody will search a courier who cannot read what they are carrying.
quests.turn_in_text:
Prynn turns it over, finds the seal, and puts it in the second drawer without opening the letter.

Fortieth. Forty-first. I countersign every one of them, because signing costs me nothing and refusing would cost me an afternoon.

And look at the seal he gave you, since he told you that you could not. That device was retired two years ago. Weezel knows that. He has known it longer than I have, and he keeps pressing it because a retired seal is still a seal to anyone who does not look.

on_accept.name: The Cartel's Complaint
on_accept.description: Sealed, and the seal is the interesting part. Nobody has opened one of these in Ratchet for about eight months.

quests.title: What Actually Sails
quests.description:
Gazlowe signs every manifest that leaves Ratchet and has signed the southern ones the whole three years, and the southern ones are the only paper in the drawer that has never come back stamped by anybody.

He is not interested in who owns Booty Bay. He wants a stamp on a season's manifest from whoever is actually deciding, because an unstamped season is a season he cannot bill for, and he would like it on the record that he asked.

objectives.label: Get the season's manifest stamped by Baron Revilgaz

quests.accept_text:
Six hundred and twelve tons, Ratchet to the cove, this season. Every ton of it signed by me and not one ton of it acknowledged by anyone at the other end.

Carry it down and get it stamped. I do not care whose stamp. I care that there is one, in the box, with a date beside it, because when somebody finally asks which of us has been running that harbour I want the answer to be in handwriting that is not mine.
quests.turn_in_text:
The Baron reads the whole manifest, which takes a while, and then stamps it.

Received. Look where I put it. The box says received, not approved, not cleared. Received.

Six hundred and twelve tons received. Say the word back to me so I know you have it, because Gazlowe will read that box and he will understand it perfectly, and he will not be able to write a single angry letter about a word that means nothing at all.

on_accept.name: The Season's Manifest
on_accept.description: Six hundred and twelve tons in Gazlowe's own hand, with an empty box at the bottom of it that has been empty for three years.

quests.title: What the Fee Was For
quests.description:
Nizzik is putting the landing fee up on the Ratchet boat specifically, by order, with a date, and she has been told to expect the small hulls to start beaching on the sand south of the cape rather than come up the ramp and pay.

They already have. Bloodsail bosuns are taking a cut off every keel that lands there, which means the dodgers are paying a worse toll to a worse collector, and Nizzik finds that funnier than she should.
quests.accept_text:
Up a silver on the Ratchet run from the first tide of next month. Not my decision and I would have made the same one.

The ones dodging it are beaching on the shallows and handing the difference to a bosun with a knife, which is the market working. Go and break that up anyway. Walk the beach track while you are down there so the carters can see it being walked.
quests.turn_in_text:
Done, and they will come back up the ramp and complain to me about the silver.

You want to know what you bought with your four. The bruisers. That is all the fee has ever been. Two enemies tie up at the same pier in this cove and nothing happens to either of them, and the nothing is bought by the week, and the week is never paid up more than a week.

That is why I do not write down where anybody came from. A list like that is a thing somebody uses later.

quests.title: The Baron Is Reviewing It
quests.description:
Aide Fipple has told four hundred people that the Baron is reviewing it. He has said it so often that he has stopped hearing it, which is roughly when a clerk starts making decisions.

Grom'gol's berth grant has been on the Baron's desk eleven weeks. The camp needs it to land a second airship hull on Authority water. Fipple has dated the Baron's own stamp and is sending it north himself, and he would like it to arrive before anyone notices.

objectives.label: Carry the berth grant to Berth-Master Zekka at Grom'gol

quests.accept_text:
Eleven weeks. I have counted. I have counted it on a wall, which I understand is not a good sign.

It is his stamp. I did not forge the stamp, I dated the stamp, and the date is the date he should have put on it. Take it up the Cape Road to the camp and give it to the berth-master, and if anybody down here asks you what you are carrying, you are carrying nothing and you have never met me.
quests.turn_in_text:
Zekka reads it twice, then goes and gets another one out of a box and lays the two side by side.

Three weeks ago. Came down with a wind-rider, different hand, same stamp, same grant.

So your clerk has spent eleven weeks thinking his Baron is slow. He is not slow. He sent this three weeks ago and let the boy keep counting on his wall, and he will have had a reason, and the reason will not be a kind one. Do not tell him. Or tell him. I have a berth either way.

on_accept.name: Grom'gol's Berth Grant
on_accept.description: The Baron's stamp, and a date under it in a much smaller hand than the stamp was cut for.

quests.title: Three Wrecks and Who Put Them There
quests.description:
Harbourmaster Sprocket's tower keeps tide, berth, weather, and who is lying about which. Three hulls are sitting on the bars off the south coast where anyone coming into the cove can see them, which he says is the point of where they are.

Two of the three are his, lost in one season to the Bloodsail. The third one is the one that keeps him up. It is older than the other two and it is aground on a bar that was not there three years ago.
quests.accept_text:
Walk out on the bars at low water. You can do it, that is what a bar is, and the cannoneers will shoot at you the whole way, so thin them first or be fast.

I want the third wreck looked at. Not the two fresh ones, I know what is in those. The old one, out on the east bar, and I want a pair of eyes on it that have never had a reason to lie to me. Go and look at the hull and come back.
quests.turn_in_text:
Cartel colours under the barnacle. I thought so and I hoped not.

That hull went north out of this cove with company coin in it three years ago and never arrived, and the bar it is sitting on did not exist when it sailed. So either it hit something that was not there yet or somebody put it there afterwards.

And in three years Factor Weezel, who files a complaint about a diary every single week, has not once asked me about a missing hull with his own company's money in it.

quests.title: Dagger-Hand Oona
quests.description:
Dagger-Hand Oona has been in the holding cage on the lower gallery for most of a year. They have not hanged her and they have not let her go, and she has worked out that this is because the Baron has not yet decided which of those is worth more.

She is not asking to be let out. She wants one name off one body, and she is offering to pay in the only currency she has left, which is what she knows about the water.
quests.accept_text:
There is a bosun on that beach who sold me to these people for a boat and a share. I am not going to tell you which one he is, because you will take six of them and one of them will be him and I will sleep.

Go and walk through the camp while you are at it. And do not look at me like that. You people came in on boats that came out of the sky. Mine came out of a shipyard in Kul Tiras. We are both standing in a goblin port a long way from where we started and only one of us is in a cage, so spare me.
quests.turn_in_text:
Six. Good.

Now listen, because this is what I owe you and I pay what I owe. The Bloodsail do not hold that beach. They hold the water. The camp on the sand is a lure and it is meant to be counted - that is why it is pitched where the tower can see it.

Everything that matters to them is afloat and off the bars, and the Baron has been buying headcounts of a camp for three years. Sell him that. Do not give it to him.

quests.title: Durgo Will Bet You
quests.description:
Crane-Hand Durgo works the hoist at the ramp foot and will tell you that standing under it once is enough to stop you doing it twice.

In the spring he put a crate through the rail into the lagoon. The crate was powder, consigned to nobody, and the manifest it was not on is being reconciled by the Baron's clerk at the end of the season. Durgo has a theory about where that powder went and he would rather bet on it than say it.
quests.accept_text:
Twenty silver says the Bloodsail are shooting at this harbour with powder that came out of this harbour. Twenty. I will put it on the rail right now.

The lagoon shelves out east and whatever goes in off the crane comes up on the rock at the end of the south beach. Go and look at the rock, and shoot the crews while you are there, and if the kegs down there are Authority kegs you win and I will pay you and you will say nothing to anyone.
quests.turn_in_text:
He pays before you finish the sentence, in coin, off his own belt, and does not ask for detail.

Right. You won. Here.

Now the sensible thing is you go and tell the clerk, because a hole in a manifest is a hole, and the sensible thing and the thing I am asking are not the same thing, and I am asking. The clerk reconciles at the end of the season. I have until then to put twenty silver back on my belt.

quests.title: A Pier Where Nothing Happens
quests.description:
Dockmaster Brek has three piers, one crane, and everybody wanting the middle one. What he sells, and he is clear that it is a thing being sold, is a berth where two captains who hate each other can tie up on the same tide and nothing happens.

A convoy is due to lie off the bars for one tide before it comes in. Oona's word was that the Bloodsail hold the water and not the sand, and Brek has decided to act on the word of a woman in a cage, which he will not be putting in writing.
quests.accept_text:
Four hulls, nine hundred ton together, standing off the east bar from Thursday's ebb. They are coming in unguarded, because a hired gun hull costs more than the cargo is worth and the Baron did that arithmetic himself.

Thin the bosuns and the gun crews on the water side, not the camp. The camp can sit there and be counted. I want the Thursday tide quiet and I want the beach track walked so the carters will use it in the dark.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four hulls in, nine hundred ton, nobody hurt, and I will not be thanking you for it because that is not what this was.

That tide was bought. It was bought on Thursday and it is paid up until about Thursday, and next week somebody has to buy it again. People come down that ramp furious about four silver and then they want the harbour to hold, and it holds because the four silver buys a bruiser and the bruiser is standing there on Thursday.

quests.title: The Road That Climbs In
quests.description:
Pilot Zan'rek brings hulls in past a reef that moves, and he does it off leading marks rather than a chart, because a chart of this coast has been wrong since the ground changed.

One of his marks is a standing stone on the upper court of the ruin inland, lined against the cape. The vine is taking it. When that stone goes he loses the only safe line into the cove from the south and the reef gets a hull a season instead of a hull a decade.
quests.accept_text:
Zul'Kundaraz. Not the ruin. It has a name, it has had the name longer than there has been a cove here, and you will say it before I tell you anything useful. Zul'Kundaraz. Again.

Good. There is one road that climbs into it and the vinecutters sit on it. Clear the road and get up to the top of the climb, where the upper court opens out. My mark is the standing stone on the seaward side and I need to know how much of it the vine still has.
quests.turn_in_text:
Standing, and you cut the vine off the seaward face, which is the face I need. That is a hull a decade instead of a hull a season and you will never meet the crews it is for.

And you said it right the second time. Zul'Kundaraz. Kundaraz is the water coming up. Not the sea, the water coming up. The city is named for a flood and it was named that on purpose, by the people who built it, and nobody in that port has ever once asked me what it meant.

quests.title: They Are Still Cutting
quests.description:
Scrip carries crates, watches crates, and sells both services at once at a discount. He also rides out on the carters' carts up the Cape Road, which is where he gets the things he actually trades in.

He has seen the Kundaraz working stone in the great court. Not clearing it, not knocking it down for the vine. Cutting. New faces, new courses, with a crew and a rule and somebody calling the measure. He knows that is worth money and he does not know why.
quests.accept_text:
Two silver for where to look, and you pay first, because I am eleven and not stupid.

Great court, the big flat one with the steps. There is a crew in there cutting stone and one of them stands back and says a number and the rest of them cut to it. Go and stand in that court and look at the faces they are cutting, then come back, because if it is true I am selling it to the Baron and I need somebody grown to have seen it.
quests.turn_in_text:
New faces. Fresh. Not patching, not robbing the old stuff for blocks. Cutting new, to a measure, in a city everybody down here calls empty.

That is four silver to the Baron. Five. You get a cut, you did the walking.

Here, before you go. Is it true the carts move without animals where you come from? Cart boys say that. They say nothing pulls them and they go anyway. I said that is a lie and they would not say how.

quests.title: Three Hands, One Grammar
quests.description:
Wind-Rider Zekki flies the only other roost worth flying to, which means she has seen all three of the jungle's troll cities from above in one afternoon: the abandoned one in the north that nobody can read, the arena in the middle that is still in use, and this one.

From the air the drowned terrace below Zul'Kundaraz is a survey grid, and it is the same grid as the arena floor and the same as the northern courts. She needs the courses measured by somebody standing on them, because from four hundred feet she cannot tell a module from a coincidence.
quests.accept_text:
Go down into the sea cave and out onto the wall-tops. The halls are flooded and the walls are the road, and where two of them cross there is a plaza wide enough to stand on. Stand on it and look at the courses. I want to know whether the blocks are cut to the same module as the arena's floor, and you will know, because you will have walked the arena.

The watch will be on you the whole way. Thin them on the shelf before you go down, not after.
quests.turn_in_text:
Same module. Three cities, three hands, one grammar, and the newest of the three is the biggest and it is under salt water.

Now the part you walked on. That bottom terrace is cut for the tide. The sills are chamfered inward, the halls have overflow courses at the top of the wall, and there are weirs in the junctions. Nobody drains a hall they built to be dry.

The sea did not take Zul'Kundaraz. Zul'Kundaraz was given the sea. Then the sea came a hand and a half further than it was given, and that part is new. I will file it. Mind the step on your way off the platform.

quests.title: What the Vine Keeps
quests.description:
The Quiet Man does not see you come in and will not see you leave, and the whole of his trade runs on that being true.

Two seasons ago he sold a buyer from the Gurbashi a set of cut stones out of Zul'Kundaraz, took the money, and arranged the carry. The carry never left the courts. A gorilla troop moved onto the stones and has been living on them since, and the buyer has been telling people, which is the only part that costs him anything.
quests.accept_text:
I sold something I had not yet picked up. Everyone in my line does it and most of us get away with it.

The east shoulder of the ruin, high side, round past where the courts stop. There is a stack of dressed blocks under a troop that has decided the warm stone is theirs. Clear them off it and stand on the terrace long enough to be able to describe the stack, and I will have a carter up there inside a week.
quests.turn_in_text:
Then I can tell him a date, and a date is the whole repair. Thank you. I do not say that often because it is not usually true.

One thing, and then I did not see you.

I do not know where you are from. I know which boat, and I know which year, because I keep both and that is my trade. So does every third person on these boards who lost something three years ago. They just do not say it where the Baron can hear, because the Baron does not care and there is no money in it.

quests.title: Salt, Worm and Rot
quests.description:
Shipwright Vella will float anything if you only give her two of the three problems. What she cannot do is make fittings, because fittings come up the coast on a boat and the boats are what she is fixing.

The drowned courts east of the cape are full of the fittings off every hull the Saltscale have taken in three years, and the Saltscale are sitting on all of it, and she is specific that she does not want the timber. Timber she has. Timber grows here.
quests.accept_text:
Fittings. Rings, pins, braces, anything forged. Not planking, I do not want planking, I have a jungle of planking and no pins to hold it together.

Nobody gets this right the first time, so: the salvagers carry it on them, on a line, the way you would carry keys. Take ten of them and walk the drowned courts down to where the water starts standing, and bring me back anything that rings when you drop it.
quests.turn_in_text:
That will put two hulls back on the water, which is two more than I had on Tuesday.

And here is the thing you saw and did not see. That pile they are sitting on is sorted. Rings together, pins together, braces by length, in rows, on a terrace. Naga do not guard salvage. They sort it.

Something down there is keeping a store, and a store is not loot, a store is a plan.

quests.title: A Hand and a Half
quests.description:
Lookout Minzi keeps the tide board at the clifftop gate, and she keeps it properly, because the one thing a lookout can do about weather is write it down before it arrives.

Her numbers say the high water on the drowned coast stands above the mark the troll masons cut for it. Not a lot. A hand and a half. She would like it measured against the mason's own mark rather than against her board, because her board is three years old and theirs is not.
quests.accept_text:
There is a cut mark on the ruin's lower wall, a line with a notch under it, and whoever cut it cut it where they expected the water to come to. Find it. Then stand there at the top of the flood and tell me where the water actually comes to.

Take the reavers off the wall first. They work that stretch and they come out of standing water you have already walked through, which is a thing worth knowing before rather than after.
quests.turn_in_text:
A hand and a half over a line that somebody cut on purpose, in stone, expecting to be right about it for a thousand years.

In three years. That is the number. Not since the masons, not since the trolls left. In three years.

I am going to put it on the board with the date beside it, because writing it down is what a board is for and the rest of it is somebody else's arithmetic. Clear to the cape, by the way. Which only means I cannot see them yet.

quests.title: What the Fish Went In For
quests.description:
Gurgle sells fish caught this morning, some of which caught itself, and works the drowned coast because the drowned coast is where the fish are. He will not go into the sea cave and has never pretended otherwise.

The fish are going in now and not coming out. Not being eaten, going in: against the ebb, in numbers, through the mouth and down into the flooded halls, which is not a thing a fish does on its own.
quests.accept_text:
Six days the shoals have gone in through that mouth on a falling tide. Fish do not swim into a hole uphill. Something is calling the water in and the fish are going where the water goes.

The ones doing it are in the halls, and they are not the naga, and I will not say more than that because I have not been down there and you will have. The myrmidons are in your way. The callers are the job.
quests.turn_in_text:
Trolls. You are telling me trolls, in the halls, with the naga all round them and not a mark on either side.

Then they are not hiding and they are not prisoners. They are working. They are calling the water into a hall that was built to have water in it, which is what they were always for, and the naga leave them alone because a flooded hall suits a naga down to the ground.

My shoals are somebody's job. I would rather it had been a current.

quests.title: The Lease
quests.description:
Baron Revilgaz has wanted the drowned terraces for three years, because a terrace under four feet of water with a hull's worth of fittings on it is the cheapest salvage on this coast and he does not have to pay anyone for the ground.

What he cannot do is sell a salvage lease on a site with a priestess standing in the middle of it. Tide-Priestess Myzrai holds the sanctum at the deep end of the flooded halls, and he is entirely open about the fact that this is the only reason he is interested in her at all.
quests.accept_text:
I am not going to dress this up for you. I do not care what she is, I do not care what she is singing to, and I do not care that the trolls down there were there first and are still working. I care that nobody will take a lease on a site with her on it.

The sanctum is the far end, past the second crossing, where the floor comes back up above the water. She will have the whole hall between you and her and she will use it. Take her out of the middle of my salvage.
quests.turn_in_text:
Good. Here, read that line before I roll it up.

The lease is drawn. It was drawn before you took the job, it is dated last Tuesday, and the name on it is mine. Not the Cartel's. Mine, and the Authority's under it, and a hundred years on a terrace that a troll cut for the tide a thousand years before anybody here was born.

Weezel will file something about it on Thursday. He always does. I will have the stone off it by then.

quests.title: Pit-Stock
quests.description:
Bruiser Kolk keeps trouble off the quay and is clear that trouble above the gate is somebody else's problem. The spit is above the gate and round the cape and about as far from his quay as this zone goes.

Four years ago he was one of the hands who walked a consignment of arena stock off a hull and out onto the sand to be held and fed until the Gurbashi sent for them. The Gurbashi never sent. Nobody fed them either, and they are still out there, and they are not stock any more.
quests.accept_text:
Raptors. Bought for the pit, landed on the spit, and left on it, and before you ask, yes, I walked them off the boat myself and I was paid for it.

Go out the spit and put them down. All the way out, not the first palm. The walk back is the same walk, so take water. And they have had four years out there with nothing coming in, so do not expect what you fought on the cape road. These ones have had to work it out.
quests.turn_in_text:
How many did you see out there. Not how many you killed. How many were on that sand.

I counted thirty-one off the hull, because I was paid by the head, and I have never once stopped being able to tell you the number.

The spit has never held more than twenty-eight. Two carters have told me twenty-eight, four years apart, and you have just walked the whole of it, and it is sand and palms with nothing on it to stand behind.

So three of them never went out onto the sand. Go and eat something. I am going to stand here for a while.

quests.title: A Pot of Something Decent
quests.description:
Keeper Marla pours inside and lets the tide keep whatever gets spilled out on the boards. She came down here from Lakeshire eleven years ago to cook for a harbour that eats standing up and has never once tried to pretend that is a tragedy.

Her stock pot wants spit crab and the crab pots at the head of the sand bar have not been lifted in a fortnight, because the boy who lifted them has taken better money on the cart run. She is embarrassed about what she can pay and says so before she says anything else.
quests.accept_text:
I can pay you badly and feed you well, and I want to be honest about the order of those.

Crab, off the sand at the head of the spit, a dozen if your arms will take a dozen. Lift the pots while you are down there so I know whether the boy left them set or left them open.

Sit down when you get back. Not at the rail. At a table, inside, like a person.
quests.turn_in_text:
Look at the size of them. The boy left the pots set, which means he meant to come back, which means I will stop saying what I have been saying about him.

Sit. Eat that.

Now. A drinker in here told me that where you come from the water arrives in the building, by pipe, hot, whenever you want it, and that nobody thinks about it at all. I have thought about that for a month. Is it true? Do not tell me how it works. I only want to know if it is true, because if it is, then you have all come an extremely long way down in the world and nobody on these boards has had the manners to say so.

quests.title: The Rate, Not the Water
quests.description:
Wind-Rider Zekki filed what she was told about the drowned terrace and expected it to sit in a box until the box rotted. Instead a question came back down the relay from a roost she has never stood on, asked on behalf of a man who keeps a sluice over a millrace in Hillsbrad and has a problem older than his village.

The question is not how the trolls flooded the halls. Anyone can flood a hall. It is how they chose how fast.

objectives.label: Weir pins off the Kundaraz Tidecallers

quests.accept_text:
Ghulrak flies a Hillsbrad that is all fences and I fly a jungle, and the two of us have been passing notes down the relay since before either of us was posted. He asked me something for his sluice-keeper and I could not answer it off a drawing.

The tidecallers set cut stone into the wall junctions. Go down into the halls and take the pins off them, then stand on the far crossing where the eastern wall-tops meet and tell me whether every junction has one.
quests.turn_in_text:
Tapered. Every one of them tapered, and no two of them to the same taper.

That is not a plug. A plug is a plug and you cut one shape of it. That is a set, and a set means somebody down there picks which pin goes in which junction depending on what they want the hall doing that week.

The water was never the clever part. The rate was. Leave them with me where they can be seen by somebody who cares.

quests.title: The First Long Leg
quests.description:
Zekki will tell anybody who asks that nobody flies out of this jungle. It is true the way the landing fee is true: there is no route because nobody has ever had a reason for one, and a crate of cut stone and a question from a stranger is thinner than most reasons.

She is sending it anyway. North to the camp, out over the water, and up the relay to the roost above the mill, which is a leg her birds have never actually been asked to fly.

objectives.label: Put the pin set in Sluice-Keeper Pate's hands

quests.accept_text:
Camp first, then over the water, then you are somebody else's weather. Ghulrak will have a bird standing because I told him to and because he has wanted an excuse to prove this leg flies.

The set goes to the sluice-keeper and nobody else. Not the miller, not the commander, not whoever is nearest the gate. Pate asked the question, Pate gets the stones.

And keep the crate dry. They have been in water. They have not been in that water.
quests.turn_in_text:
Pate carries the crate to the window, turns a pin against the light, and stops talking long enough that you start to wonder whether you have offended him.

Tapered. I have been cutting hardwood wedges for this race for nine years and swearing at them every spring, and these are stone, and they are a set.

Crank's mine. Gate drops, wheel stops, vats go cold, everyone remembers my name. That is the job, and the job is the rate, and I have been doing the rate by ear my whole life. Somebody worked it out properly and then let the sea have it.

on_accept.name: The Kundaraz Pin Set
on_accept.description: Five pins in a crate, no two to the same taper, packed in dry sacking by a wind-rider who does not trust the weather between here and Hillsbrad.

quests.title: By Ear and By Rule
quests.description:
Sluice-Keeper Pate has a set of stone pins on his windowsill and no idea what measure they were cut to, which makes them ornaments on a windowsill. What he wants is the measure itself - the thing the mason who cut them was working from.

There is a crew still cutting in the great court above the drowned terrace, and one of them stands back and calls the number while the rest cut to it. Whatever that one is holding is what Pate is asking for.

objectives.label: Notched rules off the Kundaraz Stoneshapers

quests.accept_text:
Ornaments. That is what they are on my sill and I am not having it.

Come back carrying what that caller is holding, and keep hold of it - I do not want it on a shelf in Hillsbrad where it means nothing to anybody. Take it to the pilot in the cove, the one who runs the reef off leading marks, and go down to the west end of the flooded halls where the wall-tops cross and look at how far apart the junctions sit against what is in your hand.
quests.turn_in_text:
Zan'rek lays the rule across his knee and counts down it with a thumbnail, twice, and does not hurry either time.

Same measure as the arena floor. Same as the courts in the north. And the junctions you walked are a whole number of it apart, every one, which means the weirs were not put where the water wanted them. They were put where the grammar said.

Your miller can have that. Tell him a troll had the rate worked out before there was a wheel on his river, and tell him I said it kindly, because I did.

quests.title: Kundaraz
quests.description:
Pilot Zan'rek has corrected your word for the ruin twice, and has now watched a man in Hillsbrad put a thousand-year-old answer to work on a millrace, which is more than the cove has managed in the whole time it has been standing.

He is in a talking mood and will deny it if asked. There is room on the pier head beside him, and he has carried all of this by himself for a long time, and the port has never once wanted any of it.
quests.accept_text:
No. Not a job. Sit down.

I have given that port leading marks, hulls off the reef, and the name of the city at the top of the road. The only one of the three it ever took was the marks. You took the other two north and handed them to a miller.

So ask me. The name, the three cities, and what you think your sluice-keeper is actually holding. I will answer all of it once, properly, and then I am going back to work.
quests.turn_in_text:
That is the whole of it. Every piece I have, out loud, in one afternoon.

I am not going to pretend I planned that. I would rather it had been a troll who asked, and failing that somebody off these boards, and it was neither, and by spring those pins will be in a Hillsbrad millrace doing the work they were cut for. I have decided that is better than the box.

Go on. The reef moves.

quests.title: Pins, Not Planking
quests.description:
Shipwright Vella got two hulls back on the water out of the last lot and then had to stop. What came off the salvagers was whatever came to hand, and what a hull needs is forged fittings that step cleanly in gauge from one end of it to the other.

The Saltscale carry theirs sorted on a line. She has stopped finding that sinister and started finding it convenient, and she knows perfectly well that is the wrong order to do those in.

objectives.label: Sorted fitting-lines off the Saltscale Salvagers

quests.accept_text:
Whole lines, off the belt, still strung. Not a pocketful of loose pins - a sorted line is a set of gauges and a set of gauges is a hull. Loose pins are a tin of loose pins and I have three.

Work the courts east of the cape and get down past where the standing water starts. The ones up on the dry stone are carrying what they picked up this morning. The ones in the wet are carrying what they have been keeping.
quests.turn_in_text:
Stepping cleanly the whole way down. No gaps, nothing doubled, nothing missing out of the middle.

Somebody down there is not stacking whatever floats past. Somebody is making sets up, and a set is a size, and a size is a decision about what you are going to build.

I am going to put that out of my head and plank a hull, because I have four captains shouting at me and no appetite at all for what it means.

quests.title: The Hole in the Manifest
quests.description:
Aide Fipple reconciles the season at the end of the season, and this season has a crate of powder in it that went over the crane rail and was consigned to nobody at all. He has worked out whose hole that will be, because a hole is always the clerk's.

What the beached keels handed over on the sand is written down. Badly, by men with knives, on wet paper - but written down, and a bad tally is still a tally if you are holding it next to a good one.

objectives.label: Landing tallies off the Bloodsail Bosuns

quests.accept_text:
I am not trying to catch Durgo. I like Durgo. I am trying to have a column that adds up when the Baron runs his thumb down it, and for that I need somebody else's numbers to set beside mine.

The bosuns keep a tally of what each keel paid to land. Take the tallies off them, and go through the swabs on your way in, because a bosun with his crew round him is a bad afternoon and a bosun on his own is paperwork.
quests.turn_in_text:
Fipple lays them along the gallery rail, worst hand to best, and goes quiet in the particular way of a clerk who has found the thing he was afraid of.

It adds. Not to nothing. It adds to the crate. Every ounce that went over that rail came ashore on the sand and got paid for a second time by whoever wanted it back.

I am putting this in the Baron's box myself with my own name on the top of it. Eleven weeks of counting on a wall has cured me of waiting to be asked.

quests.title: Thirty-One Off the Hull
quests.description:
Bruiser Kolk was paid by the head to walk arena stock off a hull and out onto the sand, and he counted thirty-one. The spit has never held more than twenty-eight. He has been standing at the gate with that for a long while and has stopped being able to put it down.

Every head that came off that boat went ashore with a brass tag punched through the hide at the shoulder. The tags are still out there. So is the arithmetic.

objectives.label: Brass consignment tags off the Pit-Stock Raptors

quests.accept_text:
Brass, numbered, punched at the shoulder. Goblin consignment, so every head was a line in somebody's book and every line had a number against it.

Bring me tags, and walk out to the far sand to do it, not the first palm. The ones near the water were turned over years ago. The ones at the end of the spit are the ones nobody has had a reason to reach.

Take water. The walk back is the same walk.
quests.turn_in_text:
He lays them along the gate rail, reads the numbers, and does not say any of them out loud.

They run in a block. Mine always did. Then there is a gap where three numbers should sit, and they are not out there, and I do not think they ever were.

So three head came off that hull and never went onto the sand, and I was paid for thirty-one, and somebody got paid twice for three of them. Four years I have been counting the wrong thing.

I am not going to do anything about it. I wanted somebody else to know that I know.

quests.title: The Hull Nobody Asked About
quests.description:
The old wreck on the east bar is Cartel-coloured under the barnacle. It went north out of this cove with company coin in it, it is sitting on ground that was not there when it sailed, and in the whole time since, the company's own factor has never asked Harbourmaster Sprocket one question about it.

Sprocket has stopped waiting to be asked. Every hull the Cartel ever paid for has a builder's plate riveted to a frame, and a plate carries a yard, a year and a number.

objectives.label: Builder's plates off the frames of the old wreck

quests.accept_text:
Low water, east bar, and the gun crews will work on you the entire time you are out there, so give them something nearer to think about first.

The plates are on the frames, inboard, where the barnacle has not got at them. Keep them on you. I do not want them - I have looked at that hull for three years and I know exactly what it is. Take them up the gallery, put them in Weezel's hands, and watch what his face does. That is the part I am paying for.
quests.turn_in_text:
Weezel reads all three, sets them down squarely, and lines up their edges before he says anything.

Yard, year, number. Yes.

That hull was written off in the week the road closed, and I signed the write-off, and it was the easiest signature of my career. A hull lost in that week was lost to the weather. A hull lost in the week before it would have been lost to me.

So no. I will not be filing this. I file about a diary every week because a diary cannot be audited and I can. Keep them. Sell them to the fence if you want - he will know the year.

quests.title: Which Boat, Which Year
quests.description:
The Quiet Man told you once that he knows which boat and which year, and in the same breath told you he had not seen you, and the two have been sitting badly together ever since.

He has decided to explain himself. Not to apologise, which he is clear there is no call for, but because a man in his line who is understood is a great deal safer than a man who is guessed at, and he has been guessed at all season.
quests.accept_text:
You have been carrying that since the stones. Sit where I can see the stair and ask it properly, and I will answer properly, which I do about once a year.

The book, who comes asking after it, and what it is worth. That is the whole of what I have and it is more than I have given anyone. Do not expect to feel better at the end of it.
quests.turn_in_text:
There. Now you know what is in it and what it is for, and you will have noticed that I still have it.

I am not sorry I keep it. I am careful what I sell out of it, which is a different thing and the only thing I have ever claimed for myself.

I did not see you come in. I will not see you leave. That part was never a joke and it is the only protection either of us has.

quests.title: A Long Way Down in the World
quests.description:
Keeper Marla asked you a question over a bowl of crab and then let you walk out without answering it, which she has been annoyed with herself about for a fortnight.

She is not going to let it happen twice. There is a table inside, away from the rail, and there is something on it already, and what she wants is an hour of talking rather than an errand - about Lakeshire, about this harbour, and about the thing she has been turning over since before you first walked in.
quests.accept_text:
Inside. At the table. Not the rail.

I have three things to ask and I am going to ask them in the order I thought of them, which is not the sensible order and I do not care. Where I came from, where you have landed, and the one I have been chewing on for a month.

Eat while I talk. You will not get another sit-down meal in this town. Nobody here does.
quests.turn_in_text:
She clears the bowls before she answers her own question, which is how you know she has been rehearsing it at the stove.

There. I have said it out loud to somebody and now I can stop composing it over a pot.

Come back in when it rains. Not for work. I will have nothing for you to go and kill and I will still want the company, and I would rather say that straight than have you work it out by accident.
